title: A full-B2 lower bound of 4n − (77/5)n^(4/5) for a polynomial-quotient family

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. Let L(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee.leading. Let R(n) be the sum of the monomials in guarantee.remainder.terms, each coefficient times n^exponent*(log2 n)^log_exponent*(log2 log2 n)^loglog_exponent; an empty sum is zero. There exists N such that C_B2(f_n)>=L(n)-R(n) for every integer n>=N. All remainder coefficients are the exact declared constants. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"At n=0 return 0. Otherwise choose the least prime k with k^5 >= n^3 and return 0 if k >= n. The first k input bits are the low coefficients of a monic binary polynomial Q of degree k. In F2[Z]/(Q) encode the other n-k bits in r=ceil((n-k)/k) successive blocks X_i, padding on the right by zeros, with low coefficients first throughout. For i=1,...,r set b_i=r+1-i. Return the constant coefficient of the degree-less-than-k representative of the elementary symmetric polynomial of order ceil(sqrt(r)) in the r elements X_i^(2^b_i-1).","guarantee":{"kind":"eventual_lower_bound","leading":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"remainder":{"kind":"explicit","terms":[{"coefficient":{"denominator":"5","numerator":"77"},"exponent":{"denominator":"5","numerator":"4"},"log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}}]}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one total uniformly polynomial-time family, in NP with empty witnesses, every sufficiently large integer n satisfies C_B2(f_n) >= 4n - (77/5)n^(4/5) for exact, single-output circuits over all sixteen binary truth tables at actual input length n. In particular the all-length liminf of C_B2(f_n)/n is at least 4.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v2"}

claims: In a finite field K of prime degree k over F2, the products of elements of two nonzero binary subspaces A and B span a binary space of dimension at least min(k, dim A + dim B - 1).
